sources.citation: Ambatu, Solomon Dantawaye. 2021. A Contrastive Study of English and Adara Tenses and Aspects: A Case of Ewa Dialect. PhD thesis, Department of English and Literary Studies, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria. 274 pp. (Kubanni handle 123456789/12641) [= A's work 5, re-reported because I opened it and it does carry tone remarks, for another variety]
sources.note: Incidental remarks by a native-speaker syntactician, not a phonological analysis: tone is lexically contrastive and carries grammatical functions (determiners, plural, interrogatives) in Ewa/Adara. The words stress/stressed occur only in the English-grammar sense (auxiliary emphasis). Nothing whatsoever on Idon/Ajiya prosody.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2009. The Eda [= Kadara] language of Central Nigeria [draft circulated for comment; printout July 5, 2009]: Eda-English-Hausa wordlist with introduction. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 16 pp. (= 'Blench 2009b' in Decker, Riepe & Sylvanus 2022; = A.works[0], which A left unfetched).
sources.note: Sec. 3.3 'Tones' (p. 4): Eda has three level tones (High marked with acute, Mid unmarked, Low marked with grave) and rising (Low-High, Low-Mid, Mid-High) and falling (High-Low, High-Mid, Mid-Low) contour tones; the many glide tones are attributed to recent segmental reduction. Sec. 3.2 (p. 3): homorganic nasal prefixes are, 'with a very few exceptions', not tone-bearing. The wordlist (pp. 5-16) is tone-marked on that convention. No mention of stress, accent or pitch accent anywhere.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. The Kuturmi Language of Central Nigeria and its Affinities. Draft manuscript circulated for comment, printout dated January 3, 2006. Cambridge: Mallam Dendo. 23 pp. (Glottolog ref 13802; listed by Glottolog as a wordlist; Kuturmi [khj])
sources.note: Nothing. Section 3 'Phonology' (p. 2-3) says the phonology 'is based on rapid observations and should therefore be regarded as tentative', gives a seven-vowel chart (3.1) and a consonant chart (3.2); the heading '3.3 Tones' is followed immediately by '4. Morphology' with no content. Sections 2.1, 2.3, 2.4, 4.1 and 5 are likewise empty headings. The 400+-item wordlist (pp. 3-21) is from an orthographic list written by Akubung Agayi in the mid-1970s and carries no tone marking on the Kuturmi forms (the few diacritics in the file are on cited Kulu comparanda). No statement on stress or accent an…
